lens: The cerebrovascular protection afforded by SGLT2 inhibitors appears to be comparator-specific, with a clinically significant divergence between effects when benchmarked against DPP-4 inhibitors versus broader non-SGLT2 inhibitor classes, suggesting a mechanism not fully explained by glycemic control. Concurrently, the paradox of increased hypotension risk with non-selective agents underscores a need to dissect pharmacological heterogeneity within the SGLT2 inhibitor class itself.
known_to_ignore: SGLT2 inhibitors lower HbA1c by 0.6-0.8% without increasing hypoglycemia risk.
SGLT2 inhibitors reduce the risk of serious heart failure events by 25-40%.
tensions: Fact 182560 (stroke HR 0.83 vs. non-SGLT2 inhibitors) versus Fact 186175 (hypotension OR 1.87 with non-selective SGLT2 inhibitors) creates an efficacy-safety paradox requiring mechanistic explanation.

Fact 139392 (20% CV death/HF reduction in non-diabetic HF patients) exists alongside predominantly type 2 diabetes-focused stroke and HF data, indicating a potential knowledge gap in therapeutic generalization.
gaps: Cerebrovascular outcomes in patient subgroups with both type 2 diabetes and hypertension, where hypotension risk may negate benefits.
Dose-specific hypotension risk stratification for non-selective SGLT2 inhibitors like canagliflozin versus selective agents like empagliflozin.
Long-term neurological outcomes (e.g., dementia, cognitive decline) in SGLT2 inhibitor users, given the alpha hints on brain penetration.

theses.title: Comparator-Dependent Stroke Risk Reduction: A Systematic Review of SGLT2 Inhibitors versus DPP-4 Inhibitors and Broader Non-SGLT2 Therapies
theses.rationale: This review would synthesize the specific stroke risk data from Pharmacological Research (2021) comparing SGLT2 inhibitors to DPP-4 inhibitors and non-SGLT2 inhibitors, highlighting differential outcomes that could inform comparator choice in clinical guidelines.

theses.title: Resolving the Hypotension-Cerebroprotection Paradox: Risk Stratification by SGLT2 Inhibitor Selectivity
theses.rationale: By juxtaposing the stroke reduction data with the hypotension risk data for non-selective agents, this paper would propose a framework for personalized therapy based on pharmacological selectivity and patient cardiovascular profile.

theses.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors for Heart Failure Management Beyond Diabetes: A Focused Analysis of Non-Diabetic Cohorts
theses.rationale: Leveraging the unique data from JAHA (2021) on non-diabetic HF patients and the aggregate trial data, this analysis would quantify the effect size in this underrepresented subgroup, challenging the diabetes-centric therapeutic paradigm.

reviewer_objections: The stroke reduction comparison (Facts 182560 vs 182559) may confound by unmeasured differences in baseline cardiovascular risk or concurrent medication use between comparator arms.
Hypotension risk (Fact 186175) is reported only for non-selective SGLT2 inhibitors; generalizing this to the entire class is unsupported without data on selective agents.
The heart failure evidence for non-diabetic patients (Fact 139392) relies on a single journal publication; broader replication is needed to confirm external validity.
next_extractions: Neurological endpoints (e.g., cognitive function, dementia incidence) in SGLT2 inhibitor clinical trials, focusing on brain-penetrant agents.
Head-to-head trials comparing selective (e.g., empagliflozin) versus non-selective SGLT2 inhibitors on hypotension and stroke outcomes.
